lessons.body:
Server State and Cache Mental
Model
Know what TanStack Query owns - and what it does not

Phase 22 - TanStack Query
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

Four different kinds of frontend state
A common React mistake is to place every changing value into component state. TaskFlow now has
enough complexity that this becomes harmful. The important question is not “does this value change?”
but “who owns the truth?”

State                     Examples                                         Owner

Server state              Task rows, total count, Task detail              NestJS/PostgreSQL; cached by TanStack
Query

URL state                 page, search, status, sort                       URL/searchParams

Form state                title being edited, dirty fields, field errors   React Hook Form

UI state                  mobile menu open, local dialog tab               React component

Wrong mental model                                           Better mental model

fetch into useEffect                                     query describes remote data

copy response into useState                                      cache stores last result

manual loading flag                                      URL describes collection view

manual refresh everywhere                                     form owns unsaved input

Cache is not the database
The query cache is a performance and synchronization layer. It can become stale. It can be cleared. It
can be garbage collected. PostgreSQL remains authoritative. This means the application should be
designed to tolerate refetching rather than treating cached objects as permanent local records.

Queries versus mutations
A query reads asynchronous data. A mutation performs a server-side effect such as create, update,
delete, approve or assign. A POST can technically be used as a query if it is only a read transport, but
TaskFlow follows HTTP semantics and uses mutations for writes.

Do not duplicate server state

Avoid copying query.data into useState just to render it. Doing so creates two sources of truth and makes
refetches harder to reason about.

lessons.body:
Query Keys and Query Options
Design cache identity before writing hooks

Phase 22 - TanStack Query
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

A query key is the identity of cached data
If two requests can return different data, they must not accidentally share the same key. TanStack
Query requires top-level array keys and hashes serializable key contents deterministically.

export const taskKeys = {
all: ["tasks"] as const,
lists: () => [...taskKeys.all, "list"] as const,
list: (query: TaskListQuery) =>
[...taskKeys.lists(), query] as const,
details: () => [...taskKeys.all, "detail"] as const,
detail: (id: string) => [...taskKeys.details(), id] as const,
};

Variables used by queryFn belong in the key
taskKeys.list({
page: 2,
pageSize: 20,
status: "IN_PROGRESS",
search: "payroll",
})

Page, search, status, priority and sort affect the returned collection, so they belong in the list key. If
you omit one, the cache can return data produced under different inputs.

Use queryOptions for reusable contracts
import { queryOptions } from "@tanstack/react-query";

export function taskListOptions(query: TaskListQuery) {
return queryOptions({
queryKey: taskKeys.list(query),
queryFn: () => fetchTasks(query),
staleTime: 30_000,
});
}

queryOptions keeps the key and fetch function together. The same definition can later be used by
useQuery, prefetchQuery and cache operations.

Do not put access tokens in query keys

Keys are cache identifiers and debugging surfaces. Never include bearer tokens, refresh tokens, passwords or
secrets. Authentication is transport context, not data identity.

Prefix invalidation
The key factory makes broad-but-targeted invalidation easy: invalidating taskKeys.lists() refreshes
every cached Task collection without also invalidating unrelated resources.

lessons.body:
useQuery, Freshness, Retries and
Background Refetch
Read server state without recreating fetch lifecycle by hand

Phase 22 - TanStack Query
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

useQuery is a state machine for one remote
dependency
const tasksQuery = useQuery(taskListOptions(query));

if (tasksQuery.isPending) return <TaskListSkeleton />;
if (tasksQuery.isError) return <TaskListError error={tasksQuery.error} />;

return <TaskTable tasks={tasksQuery.data.data} />;

Pending is not the same as fetching
Signal                           Meaning

isPending                        No successful data is available yet

isFetching                       A fetch is currently running, including background refetch

isError                          The query reached an error result

dataUpdatedAt                    When successful cached data last changed

This lets the page keep showing useful data during a background refresh instead of replacing the whole
table with a spinner.

Cached successful Tasks

Freshness window expires

Window focus / mount / explicit invalidation

Background refetch

UI keeps old data until replacement succeeds

Retry policy should understand HTTP semantics

function shouldRetry(failureCount: number, error: unknown) {
if (error instanceof ApiClientError) {
if ([400, 401, 403, 404, 409].includes(error.status)) return false;
}
return failureCount < 2;
}

Retrying an authorization failure does not create permission. Retrying malformed input does not fix it.
Transient network and server failures are better retry candidates.

Background refresh is a feature

Do not flash the whole page back to a first-load skeleton every time isFetching becomes true. A subtle refresh
indicator can communicate activity while preserving the last successful result.

Think in freshness transitions
A successful query can be fresh, later become stale, remain visible while a refetch runs, and then
receive a newer successful value. Stale does not mean unusable. It means TanStack Query may seek a
newer answer according to its configured triggers.

Situation                             What the user should usually see

First visit, no cache                 Purposeful skeleton or pending state

Fresh cache                           Immediate data, no unnecessary request

Stale cache + refetch                 Existing table plus subtle refreshing feedback

Refetch fails but old data exists     Keep useful data and offer retry

No data and final failure             Dedicated error state

lessons.body:
Pagination, Filters and URL State
Let URL state describe the collection while Query handles remote data

Phase 22 - TanStack Query
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

The URL still owns filters and page number
TanStack Query should not replace the Phase 15/20 URL architecture. Search, status, sort and page are
navigational state. They belong in search parameters so the view remains refreshable, bookmarkable
and shareable.

URL: ?status=DONE&page=3

Next.js searchParams

normalized TaskListQuery

taskKeys.list(query)

TanStack Query cache entry

NestJS collection API

Every page gets a separate cache entry
["tasks", "list", { page: 1, pageSize: 20, status: "DONE" }]
["tasks", "list", { page: 2, pageSize: 20, status: "DONE" }]

Keep previous page visible during navigation
import { keepPreviousData, useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";

const result = useQuery({
...taskListOptions(query),
placeholderData: keepPreviousData,
});

When the key changes from page 1 to page 2, the second page is a distinct query. keepPreviousData
lets the previous successful result remain visible while the new page is fetched and exposes
isPlaceholderData so Next can be disabled until the next page is known.

Reset page when filter identity changes

If a user is on page 8 and changes status or search, navigation should normally set page back to 1.
That remains URL logic, not cache logic.

Do not make the key enormous by accident

Use a normalized query object containing only values that affect the API response. Do not insert router objects,
functions, class instances or access tokens into a query key.

Prefetch the likely next page - only when justified
Once pagination is stable, TaskFlow can prefetch page N+1 when metadata says a next page exists.
This can make navigation feel instant. It is an optimization, not a correctness requirement, and should
not multiply requests for pages the user is unlikely to visit.

if (result.data.meta.hasNextPage) {
queryClient.prefetchQuery(
taskListOptions({ ...query, page: query.page + 1 }),
);
}

Because the next page has its own query key, prefetching warms exactly that cache entry without
replacing the currently displayed page.

lessons.body:
Next.js App Router Prefetch and
Hydration
Keep server rendering while gaining a live client cache

Phase 22 - TanStack Query
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

Preserve Server Components with hydration
A common migration mistake is adding useQuery directly to a page and converting the entire route to a
Client Component. Next.js App Router and TanStack Query can work together: the Server Component
can prefetch, dehydrate the cache, and a smaller Client Component can subscribe to the same query.

Next.js Server Component

request-scoped QueryClient

prefetchQuery(taskListOptions)

dehydrate(queryClient)

HydrationBoundary

Client TasksScreen useQuery

// app/(app)/tasks/page.tsx - Server Component
import { dehydrate, HydrationBoundary } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { getQueryClient } from "@/lib/query/get-query-client";

export default async function TasksPage({ searchParams }: PageProps) {
const query = normalizeTaskSearchParams(await searchParams);
const queryClient = getQueryClient();

await queryClient.prefetchQuery(taskListOptions(query));

return (
<HydrationBoundary state={dehydrate(queryClient)}>
<TasksScreen query={query} />
</HydrationBoundary>
);
}

Server authentication context matters

The server-side query function must be able to forward the current Supabase access token to NestJS.
The browser query function can acquire the browser session token. Keep these transport details behind
environment-appropriate API client helpers rather than making every component understand cookies
and bearer headers.

Set a non-zero staleTime for hydrated data
Without a freshness window, the client can immediately consider the hydrated result stale and refetch
as soon as it mounts. The official App Router guidance recommends a staleTime above zero for this
pattern.

Data ownership warning

Avoid rendering the same mutable query data independently in a Server Component and a Client Component if
the client can later refetch it. The two surfaces can drift. Prefer the Server Component as a preloader and the
Client Component as the owner of data that will revalidate in the browser.

Do not prefetch everything
Server prefetch is most valuable for above-the-fold data that materially improves the first render.
Low-priority panels can remain ordinary client queries. Prefetching every possible query increases
server work and hydration payload without necessarily improving the experience.

Data                                     Likely strategy

Primary Task table                       Server prefetch + hydrate

Task detail needed for initial route     Prefetch detail

Hidden advanced panel                    Client query when opened

Rare admin diagnostics                   Fetch on demand

lessons.body:
Authentication, Cache Isolation
and Privacy
Treat logout as a data-boundary event, not just a navigation action

Phase 22 - TanStack Query
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

Cached data can be sensitive
A browser QueryClient can outlive individual route components. If user A signs out and user B signs in
without a full browser reload, stale cache entries must not become an accidental cross-account
disclosure.

User A loads authorized Tasks

Tasks stored in browser QueryCache

User A signs out

queryClient.clear()

Supabase session cleared

User B starts with empty application cache

export async function signOutTaskFlow(queryClient: QueryClient) {
await supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: "local" });
queryClient.clear();
window.location.assign("/sign-in");
}

Do query keys need the user ID?
Sometimes tenant/user context belongs in a query key because it changes the requested resource.
However, adding user IDs everywhere is not a substitute for clearing security-sensitive caches on auth
transitions. TaskFlow treats logout as a cache lifecycle boundary.

401 handling
A query that receives 401 should not retry repeatedly. The API client should surface an ApiClientError;
retry policy returns false; the UI can start session recovery or redirect to sign-in. Authorization failures
(403) should remain visible as permission outcomes, not auth-refresh loops.

Never persist auth-bearing cache casually

Phase 22 does not enable localStorage persistence for QueryCache. Persisting cached business data introduces
privacy, staleness and logout-cleanup responsibilities that should be justified by a concrete offline requirement.

Account-transition checklist
Event                                 Cache action

Local sign-out                        Clear QueryClient before or with redirect

Session becomes invalid               Stop retries; recover auth; clear sensitive cache if identity is lost

Switch tenant/workspace               Scope request/key and invalidate obsolete scoped data

Sign in as another account            Start from a clean account-sensitive cache

This is a privacy boundary as much as a correctness rule. A stale cache must never become an
alternate way to view data the current identity could not retrieve from the API.

Devtools, Testing and Debugging
Learn to diagnose cache behavior instead of fighting it

Phase 22 - TanStack Query
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

Devtools make the invisible cache visible
During development, React Query Devtools lets you inspect query keys, status, observers, freshness
and cached data. It is especially useful when a query “does not refetch” or “refetches too much.”

Debug in this order
Symptom                                   First questions

Wrong list appears                        Does queryKey include every input used by queryFn?

Refetches constantly                      What is staleTime? Is focus refetch expected?

Mutation succeeds but UI old              Was the correct key family invalidated?

Pagination flashes empty                  Use placeholderData / keepPreviousData?

401 repeats                               Is retry disabled for auth failures?

Different user sees old data              Was QueryClient cleared on auth transition?

Test the contract, not the library
Component tests should verify loading, success, error and mutation behavior. Query-option tests can
verify key shape. End-to-end tests should prove a successful mutation eventually produces the correct
server-backed UI. Avoid writing tests that merely reproduce TanStack Query internals.

// Example key-level assertion
expect(taskKeys.list({ page: 2, pageSize: 20 })).toEqual([
"tasks",
"list",
{ page: 2, pageSize: 20 },
]);

Useful development checks
Open Devtools, navigate page 1 -> page 2 -> page 1 and observe cache reuse. Trigger a create
mutation and observe list queries become invalidated. Refocus the browser after staleTime expires and
watch background fetching without losing the previous successful table.

A cache bug usually starts as an identity bug

When data looks unexpectedly shared or stale, inspect the query key before adding manual refetch calls.
Manual refetch often hides a poorly modeled key rather than fixing it.

Hands-On Lab and Phase Exit
Prove that you understand server-state ownership before moving on

Phase 22 - TanStack Query
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

Hands-on lab: migrate the Task collection
Complete the lab in order. Do not start by copying the final snapshot. The goal is to feel which manual
responsibilities disappear as TanStack Query takes them over.

Level 1 - Provider
Install the locked packages, create getQueryClient(), mount QueryClientProvider, and confirm Devtools
can see an empty cache.

Level 2 - Read
Create taskKeys and taskListOptions. Replace the client-side manual fetch lifecycle with useQuery.
Verify first load, cached navigation, background refetch and error UI.

Level 3 - Pagination
Drive page/status/search from URL search parameters. Put the normalized query object into the key.
Use keepPreviousData and verify page transitions no longer collapse into an empty loading state.

Level 4 - Mutations
Move create and update network state to useMutation. Invalidate Task lists after successful writes. Do
not implement optimistic updates yet.

Level 5 - Production App Router
Prefetch the current task-list query from the Server Component and hydrate it into TasksScreen.
Confirm the first render contains data while the browser still owns later revalidation.

Security verification
Load Task data as user A, sign out, clear the query cache, sign in as user B and verify no prior cached
Task content is displayed.

Phase exit checklist
Check                             Required result

Query key model                   Every fetch variable that changes data is represented

Cache freshness                   staleTime chosen intentionally, not accidentally

Mutation behavior                 writes use useMutation and targeted invalidation

Pagination                        URL owns page/filter state; cache owns server result

SSR                               critical list can prefetch/hydrate without clientifying entire route

Auth boundary                     cache cleared on logout/account transition

Check                             Required result

No premature feature              optimistic updates deferred to Phase 25

Exit criterion

You should be able to explain why a Task query refetched, why it did not refetch, which cache entry a page
uses, and which queries a successful mutation invalidates without guessing.

Required evidence
Do not mark the phase complete just because the page renders. Capture evidence showing two distinct
pagination keys, mutation-driven invalidation, background refetch that preserves the table, and an
empty cache after logout.

Common mistakes to deliberately test
Mistake                                 Observed symptom

Omit page from key                      Different pages reuse the wrong cache

Invalidate only one exact page          Other Task list views stay stale
after create

Retry 401 repeatedly                    Slow, noisy auth failure with no chance of success

Create QueryClient during every         Cache disappears unpredictably
client render

Copy query.data into component          Refetched cache and local copy diverge
state

Debugging Workshop — Phase 22: TanStack Query

Goal
Learn to diagnose this phase's failures systematically instead of reinstalling packages, changing random configuration, or copying a fix without understanding it.

The debugging loop
1. Reproduce the failure with the smallest reliable action.
2. Capture the exact symptom: command, status code, stack trace, network request, database state, or UI state.
3. Locate the earliest boundary where actual behavior diverges from expected behavior.
4. Form one hypothesis.
5. Change one variable.
6. Re-run the same reproduction.
7. Keep the fix only if the evidence supports the hypothesis.

Boundary walk
component -> query key/options -> cache -> HTTP fetch -> server -> cache update/invalidation -> render

Start at the visible symptom and walk backward. Do not debug the database when the browser never sent the request. Do not debug React state when the API is returning a deterministic 403. The boundary walk tells you which evidence to collect next.

Failure drill 1 — Random query-key arrays scattered through components
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Failure drill 2 — Copying query data into useState/useEffect
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Failure drill 3 — Invalidating too broadly or not at all
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Failure drill 4 — Treating staleTime as data lifetime/deletion
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Do not hide the evidence
Avoid immediately clearing caches, deleting lockfiles, resetting the database, disabling security checks, or reinstalling everything. Those actions may erase the evidence that teaches you what was wrong. Use them only after you can explain why they are relevant.

Debugging exit ticket
Pick one failure from this workshop and write a short incident note: symptom, scope, root cause, fix, verification, and prevention. This is the same communication pattern used in professional bug reports and production incident follow-ups.

lessons.body:
Phase Synthesis & Independent Challenge — TanStack Query

Mission
Rebuild the capability of Phase 22 without following the exact code line-by-line. The goal is transfer: can you use the ideas when the variable names, UI, or route shape changes?

Required outcome
Use TanStack Query as the owner of asynchronous server state with deliberate query keys, freshness, invalidation, mutations, and pagination behavior.

Required artifact
TaskFlow query/mutation layer with stable keys, list/detail caching, invalidation, filters, and debugging via devtools/logs.

Constraints
• Start from the previous phase checkpoint or a fresh branch.
• Use the course architecture boundaries, but do not copy the reference implementation until after your first attempt.
• Keep changes scoped to the capability.
• Preserve validation, authorization, error handling, and observability expectations already earned in earlier phases.
• Record any design decision where more than one implementation is reasonable.

Acceptance criteria
• Can explain cache freshness vs garbage collection.
• Can design stable keys.
• Can reconcile mutations.
• Can debug stale/wrong cache entries.

Independent build sequence
1. Install/configure one QueryClient at the correct client boundary.
2. Define a query-key factory that includes every parameter affecting the result.
3. Move task-list fetching into query options and observe loading/error/success/cache states.
4. Add task detail query and prove list/detail caches are distinct.
5. Implement create/update mutations and choose between invalidation and direct cache updates deliberately.
6. Add pagination/filter URL state and inspect how query keys prevent cross-filter cache corruption.

Self-review
Compare your implementation to the reference only after the acceptance criteria pass. Differences are not automatically mistakes. For each difference, ask: does it preserve the same contract, security boundary, correctness, maintainability, and operational behavior? Keep the alternative when you can justify it with evidence.

Stretch challenge
Change one assumption: more users, a second tenant, a slow network, an expired session, a concurrent mutation, a deployment restart, or a failed dependency. Predict whether your design still behaves correctly. If not, document the next architectural improvement rather than adding complexity blindly.

Phase exit
Run the relevant checks, inspect Git diff, and write a three-sentence summary: what the system can do now, which boundary owns the new responsibility, and which failure you now know how to diagnose. Only then mark the phase complete.

Mastery Capstone Lab

This is the transfer exercise for Phase 22: TanStack Query. The detailed lessons are now closed-book reference material. Your task is to prove that the phase outcome can be reproduced from requirements, repository evidence, and debugging—not by copying a finished implementation.

Target artifact
TaskFlow query/mutation layer with stable keys, list/detail caching, invalidation, filters, and debugging via devtools/logs.

Acceptance criteria
- Write the behavior and constraints before implementation.
- Identify the owning layer and every boundary crossed.
- Implement the smallest complete vertical slice.
- Verify the happy path from outside the implementation.
- Demonstrate at least one expected failure path.
- Run the phase-relevant quality checks.
- Review the diff for accidental duplication, leaked responsibilities, missing validation/authorization, and hidden environment assumptions.

Evidence packet
Save the command/request used, expected result, actual result, one failure reproduction, the fix, and a short explanation of why the final responsibility belongs where it does. This packet is more valuable than a screenshot of a green page because it demonstrates repeatable engineering reasoning.

Stretch
Change one requirement after the first implementation. Measure which files must change. If a tiny domain change causes unrelated layers to move, use that evidence to discuss coupling before adding another abstraction.

references.preview:
# TaskFlow query key catalog

- ["tasks"] - Task resource family
- ["tasks", "list", query] - one normalized collection view
- ["tasks", "detail", taskId] - one Task detail

Rules:
1. Include every variable used by queryFn that changes returned data.
2. Keep keys JSON-serializable.
3. Never include access/refresh tokens or secrets.
4. Use prefixes for intentional invalidation families.

# TaskFlow Phase 22 reference snapshot

This snapshot demonstrates TanStack Query v5.103.1 integration with the existing Next.js App Router, Supabase-authenticated API client and NestJS Task API. It is a teaching reference, not a wholesale replacement for earlier phase files.

Key rule: TanStack Query owns remote server-state lifecycle; URL state, form state, local UI state, authentication and backend business rules keep their existing owners.

# Phase 22 test matrix

- First Task list visit -> pending state, then successful table.
- Return to a still-fresh page -> cached data reused without unnecessary fetch.
- Let staleTime expire, refocus window -> background refetch while table remains visible.
- Change page -> URL changes, query key changes, previous page remains as placeholder while next loads.
- Change search/status -> page resets to 1 and a distinct list key is used.
- Create Task -> mutation succeeds, Task list key family invalidated, active list refreshes.
- Update Task -> detail cache receives saved Task and list family invalidates.
- 401/403/409 -> query/mutation does not loop retries.
- User A sign-out -> queryClient.clear(); User B sign-in starts with no User A cached Task data.
- Devtools -> keys show no bearer token or secret values.
